application_guidance.input_pattern: Exact real-valued two-sided matvec LRA with arbitrary right-projector output and growing p.
read_original_when: Using noisy/finite-precision feedback, expected budgets, a changed confidence or a full-rank/positive-tail promise.
Transferring any source-linked imported random-matrix or algorithm interface.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Success ≥2/3 for every input; finite predetermined/all-path query cap. No confidence-dependent minimax characterization.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Universal in p≥2; logarithmic factors as stated. Fixed-p conclusions below two are a separate theorem.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact individual Av or A^T u; one product per query; b columns cost b.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Arbitrary measurable rank-k right orthogonal projector; relative error in the Schatten norm itself, not a 1+epsilon factor on its p-th power.
complexity_scope.resource: Individual products only; arithmetic and storage uncharged.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Lower covers every measurable randomized fully adaptive algorithm, without Krylov/span restrictions. Upper witnesses are inherited BCW Schatten approximation, Musco–Musco spectral block Krylov and exact matrix recovery.

content.intended_use: A minimax query-complexity reference allowing p to vary with dimension and accuracy.

dependencies: Imported interfaces as stated in this PDF: Rudelson–Vershynin [11, Theorem 1.1], Wei [12, Theorem 1.6], hard-edge laws [13,14], BCW [1] and Musco–Musco [2]
map: For R=min(N,k Phi), §8 uses Lemma 4.2 if R≤M_0 k, including near-full rank. Otherwise d=floor(eta R), with constants chosen in the source hierarchy to ensure d≥M_{K_*}k,d≥d_{K_*},d≥d_0 and k≤d/4. Lemma 3.5 embeds the d×d symmetric instance without increasing queries or residual error.

On W=XX^T, H=I−W/L, S=I−H², Lemma 6.1 gives positive s_j≥c(k+j)²/d² with probability ≥0.995. Theorem 6.3 gives theta_j≤Cj²/d² up to h=d−k−q, with conditional probability ≥0.95 before intersecting the spectral event.

For k≥K_*, Lemma 7.1 bounds Z_p≤Cd/sqrt(p). Lemma 7.2 gives R_p−Z_p≥c p k³/d² when a²=pk²/d²≤A, and R_p/Z_p≥exp(ca²) otherwise. Since d³≤eta³ k³ sqrt(p)/epsilon and p epsilon≤eta²a², each comparison contradicts R_p≤(1+epsilon)^p Z_p for small enough eta. Joint failure probability is at least 0.9.

For 1≤k<K_*, Lemma 6.4 uses F_0(t)=1−exp(−t−t²/2), F_1(t)=1−exp(−t²/2), b_0=3/4,a_0=4/5 and F_0(b_0)−F_1(a_0)>1/3. With fixed continuity loss and spectral-event intersections it retains probability ≥1/3+rho_{K_*}, not merely unspecified constant probability. Lemma 7.3 yields excess ≥cp/d² for bounded u=p/d² and ratio ≥exp(cu) otherwise. §8 contradicts the relative-error condition in both cases.

For p=infinity, §8 uses Lemma 6.2: success forces nu(P)≥9mu/16 when epsilon≤(mu/L)/8, or nu(P)≥(1−2eta_0)mu when mu/L≤eta_0 and epsilon≤eta_0 mu/L. Large rank contradicts Theorem 6.3's first mode; bounded rank uses Lemma 6.4's strict edge ratio and >1/3 event. Yao converts the fixed-cap distributional obstruction.

§9 imports BCW [1, arXiv Theorem 5.1/proceedings Theorem 4.2]: O(k log(N/epsilon)(p^(1/6)epsilon^(−1/3)+sqrt(p))) products for 1≤p≲log(N)/epsilon and success ≥9/10. The sqrt(p) term is dominated when p epsilon≤1 and costs only logarithms in the corridor 1≤p epsilon≲log N.

For p≥C log(N)/epsilon, §9 imports spectral Krylov [2] at accuracy epsilon/4 and uses ||B||_{S_p}≤N^(1/p)||B||_op, N^(1/p)≤1+epsilon/4, and OPT_infinity≤OPT_p. This gives the stated relative Schatten target with tilde O(k/sqrt(epsilon)) products; p=infinity is direct. The minimum with deterministic N-product recovery supplies saturation.

If n>m, §9 runs on A^T, forms A^T U with k additional products, and completes its range to a rank-k right projector. U^T A(I−P)=0 gives ||A(I−P)||_{S_p}≤||(I−UU^T)A||_{S_p}; left and right optimal tails agree.
proofs.omitted_details: Long Gaussian induction, full spectral comparison proofs and external random-matrix/algorithm proofs are not independently reproduced. The record preserves their exact source interfaces and actual proof locations.
proofs.reading_coverage: Original PDF §§3–9 pp.4–24 and supplied images; source-linked proof portions read, external papers not independently inspected.

assumptions: Each query chooses v in R^n and receives Av OR u in R^m and receives A^T u; both products cost two and b-vector blocks cost b.
Replies are exact. Algorithms may be arbitrary measurable and fully adaptive, with independent private randomness; computation and storage are uncharged.
Positive integer dimensions, 1≤k<N. Conditional-law arguments use standard Borel spaces and almost-every-transcript versions.
statement.conclusion: Q_p^*≥C^(−1)min(N,k Phi(p,epsilon)) and Q_p^*=tilde Theta(min(N,k Phi(p,epsilon))) for 2≤p<infinity. Q_infinity^*=tilde Theta(min(N,k/sqrt(epsilon))). Tildes suppress polylogarithms in dimension, rank, p and inverse accuracy; the lower bound has no such loss. Polynomial transition occurs at p epsilon of order one. k=N is excluded: if n≤m the identity projector is a zero-query solution; if m<n the row-space endpoint is not claimed.
statement.objects_and_definitions: A ranges over R^{m×n}; N=min(m,n). P in R^{n×n} is any transcript-measurable rank-k orthogonal right projector. OPT_{p,k}(A)=min over rank-k orthogonal P_* of ||A(I−P_*)||_{S_p}. Q_p^*(m,n,k,epsilon) is the least integer q permitting an algorithm capped by q on every input and every private-seed realization, with ||A(I−P)||_{S_p}≤(1+epsilon)OPT_{p,k}(A) with probability ≥2/3 on each input. Phi(p,epsilon)=epsilon^(−1/3) min(p^(1/6),epsilon^(−1/6)).
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist universal C,epsilon_0>0 such that for every allowed dimension, rank, 2≤p<infinity and 0<epsilon≤epsilon_0 the finite-p lower bound holds. p may vary with the other parameters. The endpoint p=infinity has the same polynomial-order minimax characterization. Probability and query cap are separately quantified as in Q_p^*.

use_restrictions: Long literature proof map only; external inherited upper bounds and random-matrix interfaces are not independently re-proved.
Exact arithmetic and free computation; no noisy, finite-precision, variable-confidence or expected-cost characterization.
